h: Which diabetes drug inhibits DPP-4?
p: Gliptins prevent GLP-1 breakdown, raising insulin and lowering glucagon with low hypoglycemia risk; canagliflozin is an SGLT2 inhibitor and pramlintide an amylin analog.

h: TB granuloma epithelioid cells (macrophages): specific surface marker?
p: Macrophages express CD14 (LPS receptor); CD4 T helper cells surround the granuloma and secrete IFN-gamma to activate macrophages.

h: Acromegaly from a pituitary adenoma: drug therapy?
p: Somatostatin analogs (octreotide, lanreotide) lower GH and IGF-1; pegvisomant blocks the GH receptor; transsphenoidal surgery is first line.

h: Anosmia with absent puberty: diagnosis?
p: Failure of GnRH neuron migration from the olfactory placode causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia; LH, FSH and testosterone are low.

h: Motile pear-shaped organisms in a pregnant woman: treatment?
p: Trichomonas vaginalis (frothy green discharge, strawberry cervix) is treated with metronidazole, which is safe in pregnancy; treat the partner.

h: Bilateral leg swelling worse at night, hemosiderin staining, varicose veins: cause?
p: Chronic venous insufficiency causes edema, hyperpigmentation (hemosiderin), and stasis ulcers; treat with compression.

h: Facial swelling and dark urine after a sore throat: urinalysis finding?
p: Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis: nephritic syndrome with RBC casts, low C3, hypertension and edema, 1-3 weeks after pharyngitis.

h: Primary hyperhidrosis: effective drug?
p: Sweat glands are cholinergic (sympathetic), so antimuscarinics (glycopyrrolate, oxybutynin) reduce sweating; topical aluminum chloride is first line.

h: Which cell secretes Mullerian-inhibiting substance (AMH) to remove the uterus in males?
p: Sertoli cells make AMH (regressing Mullerian ducts) and inhibin; Leydig cells make testosterone, which maintains Wolffian structures.

h: Pancreatitis with severe hypertriglyceridemia: skin finding?
p: Triglycerides above 1000 mg/dL cause pancreatitis and eruptive xanthomas; treat with fibrates, insulin and plasmapheresis in severe cases.

h: Pleuritic chest pain with diffuse ST elevation 3 days after MI: treatment?
p: Early post-MI pericarditis responds to high-dose aspirin; avoid steroids and NSAIDs other than aspirin early because they impair infarct healing. Dressler syndrome occurs weeks later.

h: Jaw abscess after tooth extraction, non-acid-fast filamentous rods: organism?
p: Actinomyces (anaerobe, not acid-fast) forms draining sinus tracts with sulfur granules; treat with penicillin. Nocardia is weakly acid-fast and aerobic.

h: JAK2 V617F polycythemia vera: which value is low?
p: PV is a myeloproliferative neoplasm with autonomous erythropoiesis, so EPO is suppressed; treat with phlebotomy and hydroxyurea; aquagenic pruritus and thrombosis are features.

h: Myasthenia gravis: associated anterior mediastinal tumor?
p: Thymoma (or thymic hyperplasia) is associated with myasthenia in about 30 to 40 percent; thymectomy can help.

h: Suicide attempt with tinnitus, anion gap acidosis and hyperventilation: drug?
p: Salicylate poisoning causes mixed respiratory alkalosis and anion gap metabolic acidosis; treat with bicarbonate, fluids, and dialysis if severe.

h: Ribosomes cannot bind the ER: what is impaired?
p: Rough ER ribosomes make secreted, membrane and lysosomal proteins using an N-terminal signal peptide (SRP).

h: Midshaft humerus fracture with weak grip: injured nerve?
p: The radial nerve lies in the spiral groove: wrist drop and weak extension (reduced grip strength) result; axillary nerve injury follows surgical neck fractures.

h: Thiazides act on the distal convoluted tubule, which derives from?
p: Ureteric bud forms the collecting system (ureter, calyces, collecting duct); metanephric blastema forms the nephron from glomerulus to distal tubule.

h: Corynebacterium diphtheriae: characteristic microscopic feature?
p: Gram-positive rods in Chinese-letter arrangement with metachromatic (volutin) granules; grows black on cystine-tellurite agar.

h: Primary hyperparathyroidism: PTH, calcium and phosphate?
a: High PTH, high calcium, low phosphate
d: Low PTH, high calcium, low phosphate
High PTH, low calcium, high phosphate
p: Primary hyperparathyroidism (usually an adenoma): bones, stones, groans, psychiatric overtones. Humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy has low PTH; renal failure has high PTH with low calcium.

h: Cardiac rhabdomyoma with infantile spasms: characteristic skin finding?
p: Tuberous sclerosis (TSC1/TSC2): hypopigmented ash-leaf macules, shagreen patch, angiofibromas, seizures, renal angiomyolipomas and subependymal nodules.

h: Type 1 diabetes: inheritance pattern?
p: T1DM is autoimmune with polygenic risk (HLA-DR3, DR4) plus environmental triggers; presents with DKA in children.

h: Hot, dry skin, dilated pupils, delirium after ingestion: antidote?
p: Anticholinergic toxidrome: 'hot as a hare, dry as a bone, blind as a bat, mad as a hatter'; physostigmine reverses it, but avoid in TCA overdose.
